title: Inductor CUDA graphs: distinguish compile guards, capture shapes and tensor lifetime
summary: CUDA graph replay can reduce host launch overhead, but shape specialization, pointer stability and output lifetime remain independent constraints.

hardware: CUDA devices supported by the pinned PyTorch/compiler stack
software: pytorch/pytorch at f15b476814ebc5eade36fb40512e379ebf79dd60; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: A torch.compile/Inductor path with launch overhead worth measuring
Representative shape distribution and input/output mutation behavior are known

claims.description: CUDA graphs replay fixed kernel arguments and addresses. CUDAGraph Trees manage shared pools subject to tensor-liveness and invocation constraints; eager-input mutation can cause capture to be skipped.
Shape or Python scalar guards can trigger recompilation. TORCH_LOGS=recompiles exposes causes; dynamic compilation and CUDA graph recording are not the same mechanism.

downstream_impact: vLLM and vLLM-Omni: record compile/recompile/capture events separately from steady-state latency and include diverse request shapes in the evaluation.
vllm-ascend: compiler diagnosis may transfer conceptually; CUDA graph memory and capture guarantees do not establish torch_npu behavior.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an InferRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream compatibility or performance result.
validation_plan: Freeze a workload shape histogram and compare eager with compile-only and graph replay under identical inputs.
Retain outputs across subsequent calls, exercise input mutation, and measure cold cost, graph-pool memory and recompilation counts.
limitations: A single warm fixed-shape run cannot establish service improvement or dynamic-shape stability.
Changing graph/compiler knobs may change memory use; no global mode is declared optimal.
Point-in-time source extraction, not a historical commit-delta audit. No local accelerator or model-quality reproduction was run.
